2609.29874.title: A Risk-Adaptive and Evidence-Constrained Framework for Generative AI Feedback in Programming Education
2609.29874.paper_summary: Generative artificial intelligence can turn learning analytics into personalized support, but feedback systems must decide when to intervene, which evidence to use, and how much assistance to provide. We developed a risk-adaptive, evidence-constrained framework for introductory programming using 2993 failed-submission states from 215 students. Student-disjoint models predicted persistent failure and related outcomes; four matched feedback conditions were generated for 136 cases; and calibrated risk informed capacity-limited intervention policies. The validation-selected logistic regression model achieved a test precision-recall area under the curve of 0.550 and a receiver operating characteristic area under the curve of 0.681. Broader student histories improved prediction of unmodified resubmission. After standardized repair and evidence gating, 519 of 544 newly generated messages contained all required components. A fixed-threshold sequential policy selected 17.8% of eligible test states and captured 25.2% of observed persistent failures. These findings support an evidence-gated progressive assistance strategy: calibrated risk guides intervention timing, recorded evidence constrains feedback content, and assistance progresses from self-checks to localized hints when warranted. The framework connects prediction, decision-making, and grounded generation while keeping their evaluation outcomes distinct.
2609.29874.paper_summary_zh: 生成性人工智慧可以將學習分析轉化為個性化支持，但反饋系統必須決定何時介入、使用哪些證據以及提供多少幫助。我們開發了一個風險自適應、證據約束的框架，用於入門編程，基於215名學生的2993個失敗提交狀態。學生不重疊模型預測持續失敗及相關結果；為136個案例生成了四種匹配的反饋條件；並且經過校準的風險指導了容量有限的介入政策。經驗證選擇的邏輯回歸模型在測試中達到了0.550的精確率-召回曲線下的面積和0.681的接收者操作特徵曲線下的面積。更廣泛的學生歷史改善了未修改重提交的預測。在標準化修復和證據閘控後，544條新生成的消息中有519條包含所有必要組件。固定閾值的序列政策選擇了17.8%的符合條件的測試狀態，並捕捉了25.2%的觀察到的持續失敗。這些發現支持了一種證據閘控的漸進式支持策略：經過校準的風險指導介入時機，記錄的證據約束反饋內容，並在需要時將幫助從自我檢查推進到局部提示。該框架連接了預測、決策和基於實證的生成，同時保持其評估結果的區別。
2609.29874.author: Shihao Wang et.al.
